districtFact: Albuquerque Public Schools is New Mexico's largest school district, serving about 60,000 students in 142 schools across roughly 1,200 square miles. Its family calendar combines grade-specific opening dates, conference/virtual learning days, two grading-cycle systems, and printable calendars in eight languages.

about.title: New Mexico's Largest School District
about.content: Albuquerque Public Schools serves about one-fourth of New Mexico's public school students. The district reports 142 schools spread across roughly 1,200 square miles, so districtwide dates are only one part of family planning; transportation and bell schedules are published separately because start and dismissal times vary by school.

about.title: One Main Calendar, with an Early-College Exception
about.content: Most traditional schools and Transformational Opportunity Pilot Schools follow the main APS school-year calendar. College & Career High School follows the Central New Mexico Community College academic calendar with some differences, so its students should not substitute the districtwide date list for the school's own schedule.

about.title: Conference Days Are Virtual Learning Days
about.content: APS marks its November and March K-12 parent-teacher conference dates as virtual sync/asynchronous learning days. Students are not simply on vacation: families may need to plan for online schoolwork, conference appointments, technology access, and supervision away from the regular campus day.

calendarNotes: APS uses staged opening dates, with grades 1-12 beginning before Pre-K and kindergarten. Most traditional and TOPs schools share the district calendar, while College & Career High School follows the CNM academic calendar with differences. K-12 parent-teacher conference dates are also virtual sync/asynchronous learning days rather than ordinary school closures. APS reports quarter endings for K-8, middle, and high schools and trimester endings for elementary schools serving only grades K-5. School bell schedules vary to support bus transportation. The district publishes the printable calendar in English plus seven translated editions.

planningTips.title: Planning with the Albuquerque Public Schools Calendar
content: Use the correct first day for the student's grade: grades 1-12 begin before Pre-K and kindergarten.
Treat the November and March conference dates as virtual learning days; confirm conference times, assignments, device access, and supervision plans with the school.
Check whether the school reports quarters or trimesters before using a grading-period end date for report-card planning.
College & Career High School families should use that school's CNM-aligned calendar rather than the districtwide dates on this page.
Confirm daily start and dismissal times on the school bell schedule because APS varies times to meet transportation needs.
Recheck the official APS calendar page after weather closures or district revisions; the downloadable MySchoolDates file is a one-time import.

livingHere.intro: APS calendar planning reflects a large central New Mexico district with urban, suburban, foothill, and rural-edge communities.

highlights.label: 1,200-square-mile service area
highlights.detail: The district's geographic scale is one reason transportation and bell schedules must be checked at the school level.

highlights.label: More than 140 schools
highlights.detail: Districtwide dates apply broadly, but testing, athletics, performances, graduation times, and campus events remain school-specific.

highlights.label: CNM early-college connection
highlights.detail: College & Career High School follows the Central New Mexico Community College academic calendar with some differences.

highlights.label: Multilingual calendar access
highlights.detail: APS publishes the 2026-27 printable calendar in English, Spanish, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Dari, Farsi, Swahili, and Vietnamese.

districtFaqs.q: Do all Albuquerque Public Schools students start on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. APS uses grade-specific opening dates. In 2026-27, students in grades 1-12 start Friday, August 7, while Pre-K and kindergarten students start Tuesday, August 11.

districtFaqs.q: Are APS parent-teacher conference dates days off?
districtFaqs.a: Not in the usual sense. APS identifies the K-12 conference dates as virtual sync/asynchronous learning days, so students may have remote assignments while families attend conferences.

districtFaqs.q: Do all APS schools use quarters?
districtFaqs.a: No. APS lists quarter grading terms for K-8, middle, and high schools and trimester grading terms for elementary schools serving only grades K-5. Confirm the grading cycle with the school.

districtFaqs.q: Does College & Career High School use the main APS calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. APS states that College & Career High School follows the CNM academic calendar with some differences. Students should use the calendar and announcements published by that school.

districtFaqs.q: Where should families verify Albuquerque Public Schools calendar changes?
districtFaqs.a: Use the official APS School Calendars and Grading Periods page and messages from the student's school. MySchoolDates is an independent reference and is not affiliated with Albuquerque Public Schools.

customSections.label: Which APS Calendar Applies?
customSections.content: Most APS schools, including traditional and Transformational Opportunity Pilot Schools (TOPs), follow the main district calendar. College & Career High School follows a separate CNM-aligned calendar with some differences.

APS says most TOPs schools follow the same 2026-27 calendar.
